lessons.title: The heart and its thoughts
lessons.summary: The Bible treats the heart as the center of a person's thoughts, desires and choices. What happens in the heart shapes what we say and do.
questions: Why does Proverbs 4:23 say to guard the heart?
According to Mark 7:21–23, where do evil actions begin?

lessons.title: Where thoughts lead
lessons.summary: James describes a chain: desire, then temptation, then sin. Genesis 3 shows how a single thought, accepted, changed Eve's view of what God had said.
questions: What are the steps in James 1:14–15?
What thought did Eve accept in Genesis 3?

lessons.title: Self-control
lessons.summary: A person without self-control is compared to a city without walls. Self-control is listed as part of the fruit of the Spirit.
questions: What does a city without walls lack?
In which area of life do you most need self-control?

lessons.title: Overcoming isolation
lessons.summary: Living far from home can be lonely. Scripture says two are better than one, because when one falls, the other can help them up.
questions: Who lifts you up when you fall?
Who could you encourage this week?

lessons.title: Listening and receiving advice
lessons.summary: The wise listen to advice. James teaches us to be quick to hear, slow to speak and slow to anger.
questions: Why is it hard to accept advice?
Whose advice do you trust, and why?

lessons.title: Communication and empathy
lessons.summary: Good relationships grow when we share others' joys and sorrows, and speak with grace.
questions: What does it mean to 'weep with them that weep'?
How can your words be 'seasoned with salt'?

lessons.title: Renewing the mind
lessons.summary: Paul calls believers to be transformed by the renewing of their minds, and to think about what is true, honest, just and pure.
questions: What does Romans 12:2 say not to be conformed to?
Which item in Philippians 4:8 do you want to think about more?

lessons.title: Relationships and forgiveness
lessons.summary: Bitterness damages relationships. Believers are called to forgive one another, as God in Christ forgave them.
questions: What does Ephesians 4:31 say to put away?
What is the reason for forgiving in Ephesians 4:32?

lessons.title: Don’t Chase the Butterfly; Cultivate the Garden
lessons.summary:
One day, I saw a beautiful butterfly.
I wanted to catch it so badly that I took a butterfly net and chased after it.

But the closer I got, the farther the butterfly flew away.

After chasing it for a long time, I became tired and returned home empty-handed.

Then suddenly, I thought:

“Instead of chasing the butterfly, why don’t I cultivate my own garden?”

I worked the dry soil and planted flower seeds.
Every day, I watered them and patiently waited for the sunlight and rain while quietly taking care of the garden.

As time passed, flowers began to bloom and their fragrance spread throughout the garden.

Then one day, the butterflies I had desperately chased began to come to the garden by themselves, one after another.

Life is like that.

Instead of chasing what is visible, cultivate what is invisible.
Instead of seeking recognition, develop your own depth.
Instead of chasing money, become someone who creates value.

Instead of trying to hold on to people, become someone whom people want to stay with.

Instead of rushing to see the fruit, first grow deep roots.

Flowers do not chase butterflies.
They simply bloom where they are.

Do not chase the butterfly. Cultivate the garden.

When the flowers bloom, they produce fragrance.
When there is fragrance, the butterflies will come.
questions: After reading the given passage, freely write your own thoughts or experiences in at least two sentences.
